name: SFDV
description: Explore Salesforce Metadata API dependencies directly from your source repository.

commands.title: SFDV: Show Metadata referenced in current file
SFDV: Show Metadata referencing current file

sfdv.sourceFolder.description: Folder to analyze, relative to the workspace root. Files outside this folder are ignored. Absolute and parent-traversing paths are not allowed.

sfdv.maxGraphNodes.description: Maximum number of nodes rendered simultaneously in the overview. The analyzer still indexes all nodes.

sfdv.maxFiles.description: Safety limit on the number of metadata source files inspected during analysis.

sfdv.maxFileSizeKB.description: Maximum metadata file size read, in KiB. Oversized files appear in diagnostics instead of being silently skipped.

sfdv.customRules.description: Additional declarative XML dependency rules. Each object supports id, sourceType, path, targetType, relation, transform, and optional when. Duplicate ids override bundled rules.

sfdv.includeCodeReferences.description: Detect conservative source-code references in Apex and Lightning components, in addition to XML rules.

sfdv.persistIndex.description: Persist parsed metadata indexes in the VS Code extension storage for faster scans across editor restarts. Data stays on your machine; no files are written into your Salesforce repository.

scripts.check: node -e "const fs=require('node:fs');const cp=require('node:child_process');for(const dir of ['src','media','scripts'])for(const f of fs.readdirSync(dir))if(f.endsWith('.js'))cp.execFileSync(process.execPath,['--check',dir+'/'+f],{stdio:'inherit'});"
scripts.test:ci: npm run check && npm test && npm run test:report
